Currently, `root>plain>pin` is `position: absolute` with `top: 10px` and `left: 10px`. Since `root>plain` is `position: static`, the pin is positioned relative to `root` (the nearest positioned ancestor), placing it at page coordinates (10, 10).

After adding `position: relative` to `root>plain`, the pin will now be positioned relative to `root>plain` instead. The `root>plain` element's top-left corner is at page coordinates (20, 20). The pin's `top: 10px; left: 10px` will now be offset from `root>plain`'s position.

So the pin's new position = (20 + 10, 20 + 10) = (30, 30).

ANSWER: 30,30
